category_title: Gifted student with impulse control disorder and depression exhibiting perfectionism and anger fits
minimal_context: The student is standing outside the door, being asked to transition from group play to an individual work session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for us to work individually in the office now.

STUDENT: I don't want to. I want to join my friends to play the games.

TUTOR: We need to do our work first. Please come inside.

STUDENT: (Stands outside the door, looking reluctant to work) But they are playing games right now.

TUTOR: We can't wait. You need to come inside the room.

STUDENT: (Turns away, refusing to enter and standing outside the door) No! I am not coming in, I want to play with my friends!

options.A: Move the student to a position outside the door where he is less distracted and not seeing his friends playing games.
options.B: Offer the student pieces of a preferred snack, such as a banana, to soothe him during the transition to the office.
options.C: Tell the student you will wait for him to finish playing with his friends, and then he can come inside to work on the Scratch program.
options.D: Provide visual expectations or rules, along with a visual chart displaying the time, for the individual work session.
